text: Mandi Bahauddin is a city in Punjab, Pakistan, and serves as the capital of Mandi Bahauddin District. It is the 43rd most populous city in Pakistan according to the 2023 census, with a recorded population of 232,361. The city lies at an elevation of about 220 metres above sea level, situated between the Jhelum River (12 km to the north) and the Chenab River (39 km to the south). The name Mandi Bahauddin derives from "Mandi," indicating a grain market, and "Bahauddin," a Sufi saint. In 1506 C.E., a Gondal tribal chief named Bahauddin established a settlement called Pindi Bahauddin after migrating from Pindi Shahjahanian to the area. The town began to grow in the early 20th century near Chak No. 51, where Sikh, Hindu, and Muslim businessmen and landowners settled. John Alam mapped this chak, which became the center of the new town. In 1920, due to the establishment of a major grain market in Chak No. 51, the town was renamed Mandi-Bahauddin. In 1923, all streets and roads were laid out straight and wide, and in 1924, the Pindi-Bahauddin Railway Station was renamed Mandi Bahauddin Railway Station. In 1937, the town was granted the status of a Town Committee, and in 1941, it was elevated to a Municipal Committee. In 1946, nine gates and walls were rebuilt around the town. The recorded history of the region dates back to the time of Alexander the Great, when the Battle of the Hydaspes River was fought in 326 BCE between Raja Porus and Alexander the Great, 8 km northwest of the current city, near the village of Mong on the southern bank of the Jhelum River. The Sadar Gate, built during the British era in 1933, is located at this site. Mandi Bahauddin is also the Tehsil headquarters and was raised to the status of Municipal Committee in 1941, later formalized under the Punjab Local Government Ordinance 2001. The Municipal Committee of Mandi Bahauddin Tehsil is divided into three tehsils and eighty Union Councils. The district lies in the central part of the Chaj Doab, between the Jhelum and Chenab rivers, spanning from 30° 8' to 32° 40' N and 73° 36' to 73° 37' E. It is bordered on the north by the Jhelum River (separating it from Jhelum district), on the west by Sargodha district, on the south by the Chenab River (separating it from Gujranwala and Hafizabad districts), and on the east by Gujrat district. The total area of the district is 2,673 square kilometres (1,032 sq mi), comprising Mandi Bahauddin, Phalia, and Malikwal tehsils. Phalia and Malikwal, the tehsil headquarters, are located 22.5 and 28.5 kilometres (14.0 and 17.7 miles) from Mandi Bahauddin, respectively. The district has a moderate climate, with summer temperatures reaching up to 48 °C (118 °F) and winter minimum temperatures dropping below 3 °C (37 °F). The average annual rainfall is 988 millimetres (38.9 inches), similar to that in Islamabad. According to the 2023 census, Punjabi is the primary language spoken by 79.53% of the population, followed by Urdu (17.51%), Pashto (2.47%), and other languages (0.49%, mostly Sindhi and Saraiki). Schools are present in the city.
